name: Sovereign Runtime Integrated System Test
text:
Xu's five-layer architecture helps convert the classification of sovereign local agent runtimes into an operational inquiry. The proposed system links verifiable execution to decentralized identity and state verification, adds standardized tool composition through MCP, and supplies autonomous payments through programmable wallets. These layers must operate together before an agent becomes independent of human intermediaries. That architecture independently supports the proposition that class membership should be tested against system properties rather than branding.

The correspondence remains qualified. Xu addresses decentralized economic agents, not sovereign local runtimes. The paper does not require user-held state, and it treats agent independence, rather than user control, as the principal criterion. It is also a conceptual arXiv preprint without an empirical implementation. The useful extension is therefore narrow: a claimed agent class becomes analytically meaningful only when its execution, state, composition, and settlement mechanisms can be verified as an integrated system.

sourceEvidencePassages.text: The five layers of the Agent Economy architecture are not independent silos but form a tightly integrated system where each layer reinforces and enables the others.

Agents deployed within TEEs can generate attestation proofs that (1) code executed matches an expected hash, (2) the execution environment is genuine, and (3) secrets (like private keys) were not exposed.
The Identity & Agency Layer establishes an agent as a distinct legal and digital entity, capable of acting independently of any human sponsor.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized interface for agents to interact with tools, APIs, and databases [2].
The Economic & Settlement Layer is the engine of the autonomous economy, enabling agents to hold, transfer, and programmatically manage value.
Only when all five layers function together can agents achieve true independence from human operators.
